key_insight: More images do not always improve LVLM performance: under controlled conditions, adding images frequently exposes systematic multi-image failure modes (cross-image reference errors, aggregation failures, hallucinations) that MIMIC reveals and quantifies.
problem_solved: Fills the gap in rigorous evaluation and diagnosis of multi-image vision–language models by providing a controlled benchmark and analysis that pinpoints when and why performance degrades as image count and inter-image complexity increase.
method: Introduce MIMIC — a controlled multi-image benchmark with tasks for cross-image reference, comparison, temporal reasoning, and synthesis.
Run controlled experiments varying image count, order, semantic relations and prompts across SOTA LVLMs to measure sensitivity and failure rates.
Diagnose and categorize failure modes (e.g., cross-image confusion, aggregation errors, hallucination) and use ablations to trace root causes.
impact: Provides practitioners a focused toolkit and empirical findings to better evaluate, design, and prompt LVLMs for multi-image scenarios; informs dataset creation, model architecture choices, and mitigation strategies to reduce common multi-image failures.
visual_elements: Benchmark schematic: grid of multiple images + prompt → model outputs, annotated to show correct vs. incorrect reasoning pathways.
Failure taxonomy diagram: icons and short labels for main failure modes (cross-image reference, aggregation, hallucination, ordering sensitivity) with example error snippets.
Performance chart: line/bar plot showing model accuracy or error rate as a function of number of images and task type (comparison, temporal, synthesis).
Case-study callouts: side-by-side multi-image examples with highlighted regions and model explanations showing how/why the model failed.
paper_title: More Images, More Problems? A Controlled Analysis of VLM Failure Modes
paper_authors: Anurag Das, Adrian Bulat, Alberto Baldrati, Ioannis Maniadis Metaxas, Bernt Schiele
